question: ok i keep mixing up forward reference and why it makes single pass hard. can someone explain properly, like with the logic of why the 2nd pass fixes it
reference_answer: A forward reference is a use that appears before its later definition, so a one-pass compiler may not know the definition yet when generating code. A two-pass compiler fixes this by recording declarations/symbols/addresses in pass 1 and generating target code in pass 2.

One-pass code generation is hard because the definition may not be known yet
Pass 1 records relevant information (declarations, symbols, addresses)
Pass 2 generates target code using the recorded information

required_facts: Tree edges preserve operator precedence
Multiplication groups id3 with 60 before addition
The tree is not the linear order of tokens

multiplication (*) groups id3 with 60 BEFORE addition (+).
